head_commit.message:
feat(apply): the apply flow runs the staged 4-step pipeline on both surfaces (#992)

* feat(shared): let a résumé-pipeline run start from pasted text, not just ids

resumeId/jobId on ResumePipelineRunSchema get .default('') and gain
resumeText/jobAdText siblings (same 200_000-byte cap class as the
resume/job text used elsewhere), plus small-capped jobTitle/companyName/
board for the text path's posting identity. Two refinements reject a
request with neither an id nor its text on a side. The old id-only wire
shape still parses unchanged.

The exported ResumePipelineRunRequest type switches from z.infer (output,
defaults resolved to required strings) to z.input, so an existing caller
built before these five fields keeps type-checking without edits — nothing
on this transport ever calls .parse() client-side, so there is no runtime
difference to protect.

Regenerated the Rust IPC contract via `pnpm gen:ipc`.

* test(shared): cover the résumé-pipeline run schema's id-wins refinements

Old id-only shape still parses; text-only and mixed id/text combos are
accepted; either side empty on both its id and its text is rejected; the
new text-path free-text fields are capped.

* feat(resume-pipeline): resolve résumé/job-ad text with an id-wins rule

execute() now takes a nonempty resumeId/jobId (DocumentStore/postings-cache
lookup, hard error on a miss — never a silent fallback to text) OR clamped
resumeText/jobAdText, per side. sourceResumeId is written to the run's
metrics ONLY on the id path, so a text-path run's later regenerateSection
correctly falls through source_resume_for's documented weaker fallback
(and PR-1's provenance gate still refuses to write projects from it).

Also persists the text path's job-ad text into the aggregate's job_ad
column (today deliberately empty on the id path — the postings cache is
keyed by a live job id a finished run no longer holds); the id path is
unchanged and merge_application's pick() keeps any existing job_ad.

The clamp + the pure id-wins decision moved to a new resolve.rs to keep
mod.rs under R8's per-module LOC cap.

* test(resume-pipeline): cover the id-wins resolution and text-path caps

resume_source/job_source: id wins even when text is also present, falls
back to text only when the id is empty, None when both are empty/
whitespace. job_meta_from_request reads the four identity fields off the
clamped request. job_ad_for_persist is empty on the cache path and carries
the text on the text path. Two grep-shaped checks (this crate has no
AppHandle test harness) pin that the id arms never read the text fallback
and that sourceResumeId is gated on the Store path. Extends the existing
clamp test for the five new fields.

Every new assertion was mutation-checked (temporarily broken, confirmed
red, reverted).

* feat(renderer): split the letter stream and add the 4-step pipeline mapper

- usePipelineDraftStream forwards reasoning/thinking chunks to an optional
  onThinking callback (previously dropped).
- useResumePipelineSession snapshots the draft into its own letterDraft
  buffer once the cover_letter stage starts, so letter tokens stop mashing
  onto the resume pane; also exposes a thinking accumulator.
- new pure pipelineStepForStage mapper folds the 8 quality-pipeline stages
  into the 4 apply-flow steps (analyze/generate/validate/humanize).

* feat(renderer): surface which saved doc backs the resume input card's text

Optional onDocIdChange prop reports the selectedDocId already tracked
internally, and clears to null on a manual edit (the paste textarea
previously bypassed the id-tracking state entirely). Feeds the apply
flow's id-wins pipeline run request (resumeId vs resumeText).

* feat(renderer): drop the tailor wizard's depth picker, add the 4-step i18n copy

StepModel loses DepthSelector + depthUnavailableReason plumbing (the apply
flow always runs the staged quality pipeline now) and shows an honest cost
line instead. tailor-schema/tailor-state drop depth, add resumeDocId
(wired from StepResume via ResumeInputCard's new onDocIdChange).

New pipeline.step.* i18n (en+de, label+description x4) for the coming
4-step checklist; drop the now-orphaned autopilot.apply.generatingHint/
reasoningHeavyHint keys.

* feat(renderer): add the staged-run hook and the 4-step generating panel

useTailorPipeline wraps useResumePipelineSession with the page-local UI

head_commit.message:
feat(pipeline): cover letter joins the staged run and a humanize stage removes ai signs (#991)

* feat(pipeline): reserve cover_letter + humanize in the stage vocabulary and deadline budget

Lock-chain part 1 of PR-2 (stages land in a follow-up commit): the
includeCoverLetter run-request field, the PIPELINE_STAGES union
(cover_letter after draft, humanize after repair), the humanize-tier
prompt blocks (ANTI_AI_TELL_LEXICAL/PROSE, HUMANIZE_PROSE) frozen from
@ajh/prompts, and the quality-depth deadline arithmetic re-derived for
a second streamed pass (the letter) plus humanize's flat ≤2-call
allowance: QUALITY_RUN_FIXED_SECS 4200->4800s,
QUALITY_RUN_GENERATION_PASSES 1->2, RESUME_QUALITY.run_timeout
75->90min. AGENT_IMPROVE.step_timeout/run_timeout raised in lockstep
(105/135min) so the agent controller's race against a whole quality
run still clears the new floor.

* feat(pipeline): add the cover_letter and humanize quality stages

cover_letter (mirrors draft): gated by QualityInput::include_cover_letter,
streams one letter under the run's job id via the same ai:stream channel,
no-ops instantly at zero cost when unset. humanize (runs last): counts
voice.* Warnings on both documents deterministically; zero flags is a
zero-cost finish; a flagged document gets one complete() rewrite of only
the flagged lines (never link lines), re-normalized through
projects::normalize_projects and revalidated, reverted iff it introduces a
new Critical (code, evidence) pair or more voice flags than before.

QualityCtx grows a `letter` field and `letter_text()` (prefer the stage's
own letter, fall back to the legacy request text via the new free
function `effective_letter_text`, testable without a live Completer);
validate/repair/persist/the terminal-status checks switch to it. The
aggregate's cover_letter_text is written only from the stage's own
output, never the fallback, so the merge-upsert's empty-keeps-existing
rule is preserved for a run that never generated one.

Both new fence tags (humanize_document, humanize_findings) are registered
in agent::tools::FENCE_TAG_PATTERNS.

* test(pipeline): cover humanize/cover_letter and repin the deadline ripple

Pure-function tests for the new seams: voice_count, voice_findings' link-line
exclusion, is_usable_rewrite, humanize_is_worse (round_is_worse plus the
voice-count clause it cannot express), humanize_one end to end (zero-cost
no-op, deadline-expired skip, provider-error keeps original, unusable answer
keeps original, revert on a new Critical, revert on more voice flags, accept
on fewer, and the normalize-before-grading link-safety guarantee) —
injected-closure seam, same shape as repair_loop, since this crate has no
Tauri harness to build a live Completer for a Stage::run test. Also
effective_letter_text (the free function letter_text delegates to) and the
includeCoverLetter wire default.

cargo fmt ran cosmetic-only reflow on the previous two commits' diffs. Fixed
three literal pins the RESUME_QUALITY.run_timeout/AGENT_IMPROVE.step_timeout
bump broke: paying_stages' quality stage list, the run-kind/budget-floor pin,
and the step-timeout human-readable-duration message (90min -> 105min for
AGENT_IMPROVE, both the assertion and the doc prose it was pinning).

* feat(renderer): fold cover_letter/humanize into the résumé-pipeline machine

STAGE_EVENTS gets cover_letter (drafting-family, no new state — a second
streamed document) and humanize (its own HUMANIZE event -> new humanizing
busy state, since it is quality depth's genuinely distinct last phase). i18n
en+de for pipeline.stage.cover_letter/humanize and pipeline.state.humanizing.

Every existing call site sends includeCoverLetter: false explicitly (the
generated ResumePipelineRunRequest type has no optional defaulted fields, so
z.infer makes it required) — zero runtime behavior change, matching the
backend's own no-op default. Also repins the Settings per-stage override UI's
OVERRIDABLE_PIPELINE_STAGES literal and adds the two new stages' names +
descriptions to the settings.ai.stages i18n subtree (en+de) that surface
already requires one for.

* fix(pipeline/humanize): high 1, high 2, medium, and low findings from ai-provider-expert

Addresses all 5 findings in the humanize stage per ai-provider-expert review:

HIGH 1: gate letter arm on ctx.input.include_cover_letter AND use ctx.letter
(never letter_text()) as rewrite input, so a fallback letter is structurally
never adoptable. Letter humanization is now skipped when
input.include_cover_letter=false, preventing unrequested provider calls and
overwrites of the user's stored letter.

HIGH 2: tier the usable-rewrite floor by document type:
- Resume tier: 50% floor (candidate.chars().count() * 2 >= original_len)
- Letter tier: 90% floor (candidate.chars().count() * 10 >= original_len * 9)
Letter tier is much stricter because absence of content is NOT backed by
deterministic checks, unlike the résumé validators. Document-agnostic code now
accepts HumanizeTierKind::Resume or HumanizeTierKind::Letter.

MEDIUM: move charge_daily() BEFORE entering humanize_one (not inside the
complete closure), so a Limiter refusal records a distinct capped flag (not
failed/called), and does NOT count_call. Charge refusals no longer pollute
metrics or block the correct cap/skip reason.

LOW (ledger shape): all three json!() ledger.record exits now use the same full
key set: resumeFlagged, letterFlagged, calls, reverted, voiceBefore, voiceAfter,
failed, timedOut, capped. All use zero/false defaults for unset fields.

LOW (module doc): add § Language residual documenting that English-lexicon
rewrite can seed English vocabulary into non-English prose undetected by the
per-language lexicon checks. Locale dispatch is the future fix.

HumanizeTierKind is now pub(enum) and re-exported from stages/mod.rs for test
visibility. is_usable_rewrite now requires a tier parameter. humanize_one now
requires a tier parameter. HumanizeAttempt now includes a capped field.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XR1b17ZtjMrLFnXgF9ke18

commit 22422792 addressed HIGH-2/MEDIUM/LOW but left HIGH-1 half-done and
the test suite non-compiling. This finishes it:

HIGH-1 (structural, not just the added gate): the letter arm now reads
ctx.letter directly as its rewrite input, never ctx.letter_text()'s legacy
fallback, via a new pure predicate should_humanize_letter(letter_flagged,
letter_body, include_cover_letter) — both the flag and the field-read are
independent guards now, so a future change to either alone still leaves the
letter arm structurally unable to adopt a validate-only coverLetterText.
Confirmed the persist invariant (cover_letter_text: ctx.letter.clone(),
commands/resume_pipeline/mod.rs:566-580) holds: ctx.letter can only ever be
empty or genuinely stage-generated.

HIGH-2: verified the tier split (resume 50% / letter 90%) is correctly
implemented; expanded the doc comment to state the asymmetry's actual
reason (round_is_worse's absence-shaped Criticals back the résumé floor;
the letter has no absence-shaped validator at all, so its length floor is
the ONLY backstop against content loss) rather than just restating the
numbers.

MEDIUM: verified charge_daily() already runs before humanize_one on both
arms, a cap refusal already sets capped without called/failed and without
count_call.

LOW: verified all three ledger.record exits already share one 9-key set,
and the module doc already carries the language-residual note. Reformatted
the stages/mod.rs re-export line (cargo fmt).

Build/test fix: updated all 14 humanize_one/is_usable_rewrite call sites in
pipeline/resume/test.rs for the new tier parameter (HumanizeTierKind was
added to the fn signatures but the call sites were never touched).

Added the two regression tests the ruling required: (a)
should_humanize_letter_refuses_whenever_the_run_never_requested_a_letter —
pins that a non-empty legacy-shaped letter body with includeCoverLetter
off never adopts, closing the gap HIGH-1's gate-only fix left open; (b) a
letter candidate truncated to ~60% is kept as unusable (revalidate never
runs) while the identical 60% candidate is accepted on the résumé tier with
clean validators, pinning the tier split end to end through humanize_one,
plus a pure is_usable_rewrite pin at the same ratio.

Gates: cargo test --lib (4205 passed), clippy --all-features (clean), fmt
--check (clean), gen:ipc:check + gen:prompts:check (clean, no-op — no
IPC/prompt surface touched by this fix).

* fix(pipeline/humanize): close the four advisory findings from the delta review

MEDIUM 1: charge_daily now fires strictly AFTER the deadline-passed and
empty-findings gates on both arms (mirrored in Humanize::run, the same two
checks humanize_one itself runs first), so the two reachable no-call paths
(all flagged lines on link lines; an already-expired deadline) never burn
the user's daily allowance for a call that was never going to be sent.

MEDIUM 2: deleted HumanizeTierKind. is_usable_rewrite and humanize_one now
take prompts::HumanizeTier directly (it already derives Copy/PartialEq/Eq),
and each arm of Humanize::run computes ONE `tier` value used for both the
prompt (humanize_system(tier, ...)) and the trailing floor argument to
humanize_one — one type, one value, so "letter prompt graded against the
résumé's floor" is no longer two independently-editable literals that
happen to agree today.

LOW 1: dropped HumanizeAttempt::capped — it was write-never once charging
lives in Humanize::run's own gated match arms; the stage-local `capped`
bool (already feeding the ledger) is the sole carrier now.

LOW 2: deleted the in-file #[cfg(test)] module — pipeline/resume/test.rs
already carries the stronger versions (is_usable_rewrite_tier_split_is_pinned_at_sixty_percent
pins the exact ratio where the two tiers diverge; the deleted in-file
90%-floor test stayed green under a 0.9->0.7 mutation and pinned nothing).

Gates: cargo test --lib (4202 passed, -3 from the deleted in-file tests),
clippy --all-features (clean), fmt --check (clean), gen:ipc:check +
gen:prompts:check (clean, no-op — no IPC/prompt surface touched).

* fix: address coderabbit findings on pr #991 humanize stage

- skip humanize entirely for a document over HUMANIZE_DOCUMENT_CAP instead
  of letting fenced() silently truncate it and grading a prefix-only rewrite
  against the real (untruncated) length floor
- treat a revalidate error inside humanize_one as a failed attempt (keep
  original, mark failed) instead of propagating it and failing the run
- fail closed when the letter revalidate closure produces no report for a
  non-empty candidate, instead of substituting an accept-shaped empty report
- extract the ledger's 9-key json! literal (now 10, with tooLarge) into one
  Artifact struct shared by all three Stage::run exits
- pin the humanize_findings block as the second untrusted fenced block with
  hostile content, an evidence-less voice finding still reaching
  voice_findings, and the exact resume/letter floor boundaries
- fix stale prose: gen-ipc-rust.ts's hand-authored doc comments and
  ai-timeouts.test.ts's formula comment still described draft as the only
  generation pass; en/de generationDepth quality copy still described the
  pre-PR-2 six-stage/4-call pipeline

feat(pipeline): code-owned projects section at quality depth with link-label fidelity (#990)

* feat(resume): code-own the projects section at quality depth

Add pipeline/resume/projects.rs: normalize_projects re-renders the draft's
Projects section from source-seeded ProjectOut entries (same parser the
max-depth seeder uses), preserving draft order, dropping model-invented
entries, and restoring altered/dropped links verbatim through the existing
render_project ladder. Hooked into the draft stage (content-free ledger
counts), the repair loop (normalize before revalidate), and the per-section
regenerate command.

Also preserve markdown link labels ([Website](url)) from the source résumé
through seeding so PDF/DOCX export keeps the candidate's own link labels
instead of losing them to bare hrefs.

reseed_projects and same_project move from stages/section_gen.rs into the
new module (section_gen re-imports); max-depth output is unchanged.

* fix(resume): gate projects normalization on plausible source structure

Addresses rust-backend-architect review findings on 5585026b:

- CRITICAL: refuse to normalize when the source's Projects section has no
  genuine bold/bullet entry boundary (the shape every extraction::* PDF/DOCX/
  RTF importer produces) or when seeded fields cross-contaminate each other —
  a plain-text source previously collapsed into one garbage mega-entry that
  normalization would rewrite a correct draft into, validation-clean.
- CRITICAL: an all-dropped normalization pass is now a no-op instead of
  persisting a heading-only Projects section with no undo.
- HIGH: the regenerate-section hook now only writes when source_resume_for
  found a real provenance hit, never the generated-text fallback.
- HIGH: added tests for both the draft-stage hook and the regenerate hook,
  extracting the deterministic decision out of each into a pure, unit-tested
  function (apply_projects_normalization, normalize_regenerated_projects).
- MEDIUM: the regenerate hook is scoped to Projects-key regenerations only,
  so regenerating another section no longer reverts manual Projects edits.
- MEDIUM: a splice now re-adds the blank line before a following section;
  a dedup collision during reseed is counted as dropped; resolve_seed_names
  refuses to rename when more than one seed shares a link.
- LOW: link_href moved beside canonical_link in validate::content to kill
  the source.rs<->projects.rs module cycle; build() parses the document once
  via the existing split_parsed seam; a captured markdown-link span is only
  written when it round-trips through urls_in and has balanced parens,
  otherwise falls back to the bare href; the label regex accepts every URL
  shape urls_in does (not just https://); a matched span is stripped before
  the bare-URL harvesting pass so a URL-shaped label isn't counted twice.
- Added a model::rich test proving a rendered project line's markdown link
  labels become the hyperlink text.

* fix(resume): never delete an unmatched draft project, gate on seed plausibility

Structural rework of the projects-normalization pass per rust-backend-architect
review of caef3d1c (C1 executed reproductions: plain titles + bulleted
achievements; bold titles + bullet achievements; a plain-text draft merging
two projects).

- Rule 1: normalization's write authority now extends only to draft Projects
  entries it can confidently match to a seed. An entry that matches nothing
  is left VERBATIM in its original position, never deleted or invented over
  — the validators still grade whatever it says. A second entry resolving to
  an already-used seed is still an allowed dedup drop.
- Rule 2: seed_projects_for_normalize whole-bails (returns no seeds) when the
  source's Projects section produces ANY seed with no link, no stack and no
  description — the signature of a mis-grouped fragment (a swallowed title,
  an achievement bullet counted as its own entry), which the old
  "any entry-start line" gate could not see (bullets satisfy the entry-start
  rule; the swallowed plain title never becomes a seed).
- Rule 3: build() now also bails the whole pass when a seed the draft never
  matched has its own link present, unattached, somewhere in the draft's
  Projects text — the signature of the DRAFT's own entry grouping merging two
  projects into one (a plain-text draft has no gate at all otherwise).
- Rule 4: seeds_are_plausible now compares only stack entries and links
  against sibling names/links, dropping the description from the haystack —
  a truthful description cross-referencing a sibling project by name no
  longer disables normalization for an honest source.
- Rule 5: every bail records a content-free reason
  (projectsNormalizeSkipped: empty_seed | implausible_seeds |
  draft_parse_disagreement | no_entry_starts | seed_claims_multiple_entries)
  on the draft-stage ledger artifact, so a silent skip is observable.
- Rule 6 (N3): source.rs only strips markdown-link spans it actually captured
  as links before the bare-URL harvest pass; a span the single-URL guard
  skipped keeps its own bare URL(s) reachable instead of deleting them.
- Additional guard beyond the seven rules: while testing the primary
  "N projects collapse into one seed" shape from a fully plain-text source,
  neither the empty-seed nor the plausibility gate catches it when the
  resulting single seed's merged links/description both happen to be
  non-empty (no sibling to compare against). build() now also bails
  (seed_claims_multiple_entries) when a seed the link-fallback matches to a
  SECOND, differently-named draft entry — the direct signature of one seed
  having swallowed multiple projects' links, distinct from an ordinary
  same-name dedup. Flagged here since it goes past the literal seven rules.
- max: output-preserving; the dropped-metric now also counts a dedup
  collision it silently missed before (from the previous review round).

extraction of apply_projects_normalization/normalize_regenerated_projects as
pure functions (previous round) is what makes all of the above testable
without a live provider or AppHandle; new regression fixtures encode the
three reproduced shapes as no-ops, plus a positive well-formed-source case
proving the feature still fires (link restored, label preserved, order kept,
legitimate description intact).
